messages:
noah: Heads-up: Partner Connector (FluxCorp) is sending ephemeral usage markers with seq numbers that sometimes reset after connector restarts. causing our dedupe logic to incorrectly consider them new and double-count in daily rollups.

tia: Are these seq numbers per-connector instance? any unique connector_id in payload?

noah: They include `connector_instance` in headers but the seq/restart doesn't include an epoch id. sample payload:

```json
{"tenant":"acme-eu","timestamp":"2026-03-18T11:05:00Z","units":30,"seq":12}
```

noah: WhenFlux restarts, seq resets to 1 and connector_instance header changes. We only dedupe on (tenant, seq) so duplicates slip through when instance changes.

sumit: quick fix: include connector_instance in dedupe key or require a monotonic `claim_id` UUID from partner. which is faster?

vendor-team: We're pushing a fix to include claim_id in next micro-release but ETA 3 days. adding connector_instance to dedupe might be faster on your side.

noah: Adding connector_instance to dedupe key in ingestion sounds safe and reversible. tia, can you make a small change to ingestion dedupe? log any increases in drop rates.

tia: yes. I'll add a `dedupe_key` field that concatenates partner_id|tenant|connector_instance|seq. will emit metric `dedupe_key_changes` and a debug log sample. PR inbound.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: branch=ingest/dedupe-connector-instance, env=staging, window=5m

noah: Also let's add a test harness case for this: simulate two connector instances replaying same seq but different instance ids within 2 minutes and assert we do NOT double-count. tia can you add to ingest-tests?

tia: yep adding an integ test. will mock headers and run replay.

sumit: longer-term, recommend partners include a UUID claim_id to be canonical. we'll add it to the spec. vendor-team ack.

noah: Thanks all. Action: tia (dedupe change + test), vendor (micro-release with claim_id in 3 days), sumit (update partner spec), ops (monitor staging rollout)
